title: Post-launch retro: perf-canary alert usefulness, detector changes, and v2 backlog
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Capture what we learned from perf-canary phase 1/2 rollout (us-east + eu-west) and the first real pages.
- Separate “useful signal” vs “noise/false positives”.
- Agree on detector + dashboard/payload changes for v1.1.
- Produce a prioritized v2 backlog (workload coverage + bisect hints + quality-of-life).

Context / artifacts
- Linear epic: ENG-2841 (Perf regression canary in prod)
- Detector/backtesting: ENG-2855
- Noise reduction: ENG-2852
- Alert routing + runbook: ENG-2848 / ENG-2849
- First incident thread: #incidents thread_1736821902 (latency regression event; rollback decision)
- Notable fixes discovered during rollout:
  - Streaming tokens/sec timestamp alignment (runtime PR redwood/pr_39157)
  - p95 aggregation window mismatch (runtime/telemetry hotfix redwood/pr_39249)

Retro attendees (core)
- Runtime: Noah Patel, Sofia Ivanova, Hiro Tanaka, Omar El-Sayed
- SRE: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Tomáš Novák
- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- Program: Talia Benson

What was useful (keep / expand)
1) “Hard” regressions that correlated to deploys (high confidence)
- Useful pages were ones where:
  - Regression was isolated to a single runtime_build + gpu_sku slice OR a single region with a known fleet change.
  - The dashboard annotation clearly showed a runtime deploy within ~30 minutes of onset.
  - Both p95 latency and tokens/sec moved in the expected opposite directions (latency up, tokens/sec down), rather than single-metric spikes.
- Example: eu-west, model_family=llama-70b class, gpu_sku=A100-80G slice showed p95 +18–22% sustained for >40m; rolled back runtime RC and returned to baseline within 20m.

2) Alerts that included enough attribution to route quickly
- Payload fields that materially reduced triage time:
  - runtime_build + git_sha (or at least a stable build id)
  - scheduler_mode (pinned vs default)
  - gpu_sku and region
  - model + prompt_shape_id
  - direct links: “p95 panel” + “tokens/sec panel” + runbook
- The incident-bot formatting was good enough to get Runtime engaged quickly once SRE confirmed slice consistency.

3) Canary-safe request class behavior
- No evidence that canary jobs impacted customer queues (no visible queue contention during peak hours; no SRE reports of canary starving real traffic).
- Keeping canary in the low-priority request class is the right default; we should avoid “dedicated queue” until we have stronger evidence we need it.

What was noisy (change)
1) Post-deploy warmup / cache cold-start effects (false positives)
- We saw multiple alerts firing within the first 10–25 minutes after deploy/rollout steps.
- Root causes:
  - KV/prefix cache cold + kernel autotune settling.
  - Node-level GPU clock / power state ramp (esp. after scale-out events).
  - Canary warmup step helped, but still not enough when fleet composition changes during rollout.
- Action: bake in a detector “quiet period” tied to deploy annotations per (region, gpu_sku, runtime_build).

2) GPU SKU heterogeneity leaking into aggregated series
- When metrics accidentally aggregated across gpu_sku (or when gpu_sku label was missing for a subset of samples), it created apparent regression steps.
- This was most visible in eu-west during partial A100/H100 mix periods.
- Action: enforce required labels for perf-canary series (drop samples missing gpu_sku/runtime_build instead of aggregating them).

3) “Single-metric spikes” from sampling and windowing
- p95 spikes that did not correspond to throughput changes were often:
  - insufficient sample size in the window
  - p95 window mismatch between runtime emission and telemetry rollup (fixed by redwood/pr_39249)
  - outlier bursts from node contention (noisy neighbors, background maintenance) that did not persist
- Action: raise min sample size; require persistence across N consecutive windows before paging.

Agreed detector changes (v1.1)
- Baseline
  - Keep rolling baseline (7d median) as the default comparator (per ADR-0231).
  - Add an optional pinned “known-good build” comparator in dashboards (not for paging) to help Runtime bisect quickly.
- Regression condition (proposal to implement)
  - Minimum sample size per evaluation window (per slice):
    - latency windows: >= 200 requests
    - tokens/sec windows: >= 120 requests
  - Persistence gate: regression must trigger in 3 consecutive 10m windows (i.e., sustained ~30m) before paging.
  - Deploy quiet period: suppress paging for 20m after a deploy annotation for that slice (still create a non-paging annotation/ticket signal).
  - Two-metric confirmation for paging severity S2:
    - latency regression >= +12% AND tokens/sec regression <= -8% (relative to baseline)
    - otherwise downgrade to ticket-only (no page) unless regression is extreme (latency >= +25% or tokens/sec <= -20%).
- Label/schema enforcement
  - Hard requirement: model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, traffic_class=canary-safe, prompt_shape_id.
  - For missing required labels: drop from detector input and emit a separate “canary telemetry hygiene” counter.

Alerting policy changes (SRE)
- Keep initial paging routed to SRE (triage + dedup), with auto-assign to Runtime only after SRE confirms:
  - regression persists across at least 30m
  - slice is consistent (not cross-SKU bleed)
  - not within deploy quiet period
- Add a dedicated “noise/false positive” follow-up workflow:
  - SRE files a tuning ticket against detector rules with screenshots + timestamps + suspected cause.

Dashboards + payload improvements
- Add a “slice compare” quick link in alert payload:
  - same model/region but other gpu_sku
  - same model/gpu_sku but other region
  - same slice but previous runtime_build
- Add explicit display of:
  - kernel_id + fallback_reason (when present)
  - batch composition summary (prefill/decode counts, max_seq_len)
  - cache hit-rate (if we can emit without cardinality blowup)

Open questions
- Should we compute tokens/sec based on wall time including queueing, or strictly service time?
  - For now: keep current definition (service-side timestamps) and add queue time as a separate metric panel for attribution.
- How aggressive should we be with suppression (risk: hiding real regressions)?
  - Action: backtest with and without suppressions and compare “would-have-paged” counts vs real incidents.

v2 backlog (prioritized)
P0 (next)
- Add additional workload shapes per model family (current prompt shapes are too “stable” vs real traffic):
  - long-prefill / short-decode
  - short-prefill / long-decode
  - tool/function-call structured output
- Add automated “suspected cause hints” in payload:
  - if kernel_id changed vs baseline -> highlight
  - if scheduler_mode changed -> highlight
  - if gpu_sku mix changed in region -> highlight

P1
- Add optional “shadow compare” against offline benchmark-lab slice export for sanity checks (not a gate, just context).
- Add a lightweight profiler capture trigger for confirmed regressions (rate limited; only on sustained S2 events).

P2
- Expand coverage to additional regions once detectors are stable (APAC region once fleet is consistent).
- Explore whether canary should include small mixed-load contention simulation (bounded) to catch scheduler regressions under mix.

Definition of done
- Retro notes finalized and shared in #announcements (eng) with clear “what changed” summary.
- Detector changes + alert policy updates accepted by Runtime + SRE + Telemetry.
- Create/track follow-up tickets for v1.1 and v2 backlog (with owners).
comments: 2026-02-10 (Talia Benson): Creating retro ticket per launch checklist. Please add concrete examples of useful vs noisy alerts (links/screenshots) and any proposed threshold changes before Friday sync.

2026-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE POV the biggest pager-fatigue driver is deploy-adjacent spikes (esp. first ~15m) + missing gpu_sku label causing blended series. Strong +1 to dropping missing-label samples and adding deploy quiet period. Also recommend persistence gate (3x 10m windows) before paging.

2026-02-13 (Noah Patel): Useful incident was the eu-west sustained p95 regression aligned with runtime RC rollout; payload having runtime_build was the difference. Would like dashboards to show kernel_id deltas vs baseline to reduce time-to-suspect kernel regression.

2026-02-14 (Nadia Rahman): Telemetry can enforce required labels at aggregation stage (drop + increment hygiene counter). Need agreement on which labels are strictly required to stay within cardinality budget; proposed set in description looks fine if prompt_shape_id remains a small controlled vocabulary.

2026-02-18 (Sofia Ivanova): We should avoid suppressing purely based on deploy window without still emitting a non-paging signal; otherwise we’ll miss regressions that start immediately post-deploy. Proposal: during quiet period create a ticket-only alert with lower urgency, then page only if persists past quiet period.

2026-02-21 (Tomáš Novák): Drafted proposed detector rule update in description (min samples + persistence + 2-metric confirm). Next step is to run backtest using ENG-2855 harness and post results (pager volume estimate).

2026-02-25 (Talia Benson): Please review the proposed threshold numbers (+12% latency / -8% tokens/sec) in the next cross-team sync. If we agree, I’ll file concrete follow-up tickets for v1.1 implementation + v2 workload expansion and link them here.
